Hi Sam — great to hear you’re ready to start. I put together an implementation-first checklist and some concrete guidance below. Attaching a lightweight checklist and a small zip of sample snippets.

High-level plan (recommended):
1) Sandbox wiring (2 days): get SDK auth and basic requests working against the sandbox key.
2) Smoke tests & retries (1–2 days): validate timeouts, retry behavior, and error classification.
3) Pilot traffic (3–5 days): route a small % of traffic to Redwood hosted endpoints.
4) Cutover & monitoring (1 day): DNS/route switch, verify metrics and fallbacks.

SDK setup (Node + Python examples included in the zip):
- Node (npm install @redwood/inference):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1' });
  const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-2b', prompt: 'Hello' });

- Python (pip install redwood-sdk):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'], base_url='https://api.redwood.ai/v1')
  out = c.generate(model='redwood-2b', prompt='Hi')

Endpoint migration notes (Hosted -> Dedicated later):
- Use baseUrl override in client config. Keep the same API surface (no code changes required beyond baseUrl).
- We recommend feature-flagging the baseUrl so you can flip between hosted and dedicated without a deploy.
- During DNS cutover, keep a short cache TTL on your resolver (60s) and have a fallback rule (route to hosted) for 10 minutes after cutover if health checks fail.

Retries & timeouts (recommended defaults):
- Client timeout (end-to-end): 15s for single-shot generation calls. For streaming, keep 60s socket read timeout.
- Retries: 3 attempts max for idempotent calls (embeddings / reranking). For generation, retry only on network-level errors or 5xx with backoff.
- Backoff: exponential backoff with jitter, base=200ms, factor=2, max=2s.
- Error classification: do NOT retry on 4xx (prompt errors, auth). Retry on 429 with burst handling (see rate limit section) and on 5xx.

Rate limit handling:
- Hosted API default quota: 60 requests/minute per API key for non-batched generation (we can increase for pilot).
- Recommended client behavior: implement a local token-bucket limiter (burst capacity 5x, refill rate = steady-state rate).
- On receiving 429: parse Retry-After header if present; if missing, apply exponential backoff + jitter and reduce concurrency by 50% for subsequent window.

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (checklist + smoke tests), sdk-sample-snippets.zip (Node/Python/curl examples).

I’m looping Marcus and Karthik for any low-level networking notes and to confirm rate-limit numbers for your pilot.

Hey all — a few engineering-specific notes to complement Naomi’s guidance: 

Network / firewall:
- Outbound to api.redwood.ai (443) is required. We publish a small set of egress IPs for Hosted; see the linked doc. If you prefer an IP allowlist we can provide the current CIDR block (subject to change with notification).
- Health checks: we recommend a simple /v1/health ping every 30s during cutover.

Concurrency & batching:
- If you’ll be doing many short requests (embeddings / short prompts) enable batching client-side (we include a batching helper in the SDK). Aim for batch sizes of 8–32 depending on payload size.
- Max concurrent generation requests per worker: start at 4 and tune up. We saw CPU/latency degradation above ~12 concurrent on 8GB worker VMs.

Headers & observability: include these headers to make debugging easier:
- X-Redwood-Request-ID: echo from client (UUID)
- X-Client-App: brightline-platform
- X-Trace-Id: optional application trace id

Small examples (copied from the snippets zip):
- cURL (generate):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","prompt":"Summarize sales notes"}'

- Node batching helper (pseudo):
  const b = new Redwood.Batcher({maxSize: 16, intervalMs: 50});
  b.enqueue({prompt: 'A'});

If you want, we can run a short 1-hour workshop with your SRE to walk through traffic shaping and firewall rules this week.

Priya / Sam — quick answers and confirmations: 

- Retry-After: we respect either integer-seconds or HTTP-date. Our SDKs parse both; hosted will return seconds when possible.
- Batching accounting: token accounting is per-request but billing is aggregated per HTTP call for batched requests (you’ll see total tokens consumed for the batch).
- Cutover support: Nov 12, 10–11 PST works; I’ll be on the call, Marcus will standby for network checks, and Karthik will join for SDK troubleshooting.

Next steps:
- We’ll schedule a 45-minute prep session (Thu Nov 11, 10:00 PST) to run health checks and test keys.
- You’ll receive a prod API key the morning of Nov 12 once we confirm the smoke tests.
